newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher's Xmas cheer prompts upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher's Xmas cheer prompts upgrades.

text.p: Strong Christmas trading from Woolworths and Comet prompted a rash of profit forecast upgrades for British retail group Kingfisher Plc on Wednesday.

Retail analysts said UBS had raised its forecast for the current year by 10 million to 380 million stg. Roy Maconochie at Henderson Crosthwaite was already predicting 380 million stg for the current year but said he would increase his forecast for the 1997/98 financial year to 445 million stg from 435 million.
Victoria Melendez at Morgan Stanley said she would raise her forecast in the light of the group's strong trading but had not finalised the numbers.
Analysts said aggressive pricing by Woolworths had probably won Kingfisher some market share from rival Argos Plc over Christmas, especially on toys.
Last year it was probably a draw between Woolworths and Argos in terms of Christmas sales, Maconochie said. "This year in football parlance it was probably three nil to Kingfisher," he said.

Electricals chain Comet also performed well with like for like sales up 14 percent in the nine weeks to January 4. But analysts said this compared with a relatively sluggish performance over last Christmas.

Analysts said higher costs from advertising and depreciation related to new-style stores at Superdrug, the personal care chain, were a negative factor. But home decor chain B&Q performed well and analysts see more improvments to come from its store refurbishment programme.
Profit-taking hit the group's shares as Christmas cheer was already in the price, analysts said. But they expected the stock to recover in the run up to final results in March.

Several analysts recommended the shares as a buy, arguing they are at a discount to the stores sector and could make headway above 700 pence. Others have them as a hold. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
